reviewer_scope: same-workflow second-pass static review; not an independent reviewer

findings.evidence: Stock Ghidra shows the callback transitions phase 1->2->3 and fan_speed_show writes phase 1 before arming the hrtimer. Candidate callback uses READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE; fan_speed_show remains a hand-authored instruction body.
findings.assessment: Callback annotations preserve single-copy compiler semantics for its C accesses. They do not serialize a delayed callback against a later sysfs sample; the one-second wait and timer behavior remain stock. This review does not claim the callback always runs before the sysfs read.

findings.evidence: The stock IRQ body increments the aligned 32-bit counter using the AArch64 LSE/LL-SC atomic path. The timer callback uses atomic_set/atomic_read for reset and observations; its assembly comparison is exact.
findings.assessment: The access width and offset are aligned. The IRQ update is inline assembly, so this static review cannot claim KCSAN instrumentation or a runtime race-free result.

findings.evidence: The callback publishes the 32-bit snapshot with WRITE_ONCE after reading the counter. Stock fan_speed_show sleeps for one second and then reads the snapshot; it does not cancel the timer before that read.
findings.assessment: If timer execution is delayed, the read can observe a previous snapshot, as in stock. Adding cancellation, completion, or a new lock would alter timing/control flow and is not justified by this parity-only review.

findings.evidence: The current remove path cancels the hrtimer before clearing driver state and releasing the context.
findings.assessment: This supports the teardown ordering statically; runtime timing and hardware behavior remain unverified.

decision: No source change or status promotion is justified. Preserve stock-matched timing and record the delayed-timer residual.

build_validation.basis: The existing two-cycle Docker report is hash-bound to the unchanged current source and module; this batch changes documentation only.

limitations: No new KCSAN, runtime, or NX809J hardware validation.
Whole-driver audit remains incomplete; other intentional hardening deviations remain.
